subject: Post-call: model fit & multilingual evals next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@globex.de>, Tariq Hassan <tariq.hassan@globex.de>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Hi Anna / Tariq —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary goal: replace current translation + NLU pipeline for customer support triage across DE/FR/ES and Japanese/Korean with a single multilingual LLM-powered flow.
- Key constraints: strict PII handling, EU data residency for EU traffic, and latency SLOs for peak hours in APAC.
- Success metrics: intent classification accuracy >= 92% (per locale) and reduction in average handling time by 20%.

What we promised to deliver by next week: 
1) Candidate model recommendations and a short eval plan targeted at DE/FR/ES/JA/KO.
2) A small prompt set (100 examples across locales) and instructions for running a quick closed-loop eval.
3) Initial benchmark link and a summary of expected latency/throughput on Dedicated capacity.

I've attached the initial eval report and prompt set (redwood-eval-report.pdf, prompt-sets.csv) and shared the Drive folder with your team: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-Globex-evals

Recommended models for the first pass: 
- redwood-multilingual-2.0 (best quality across EU languages)
- rwd-quant-4bit-multilang (cost-effective for high-throughput latency-sensitive endpoints)

Next steps (proposed):
- You/your data team share a small sample of anonymized transcripts (we can accept via secure upload link or S3 with customer-managed keys).
- Redwood will run the prompt set against both models above and return per-locale confusion matrices + regression notes.

Would Thursday (3/25) 10:00 AM CET work for a sync to review results?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood-eval-report.pdf (summary PDF)
Attachment: prompt-sets.csv (100-example prompt set, locale labels)

From: Anna Müller <anna.muller@globex.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tariq Hassan <tariq.hassan@globex.de>
Date: 2027-03-21T08:23:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed.

A few clarifications from our side:
- We can provide a 500-row anonymized export for the five target locales by Tue EOD (3/23). Will include intent labels.
- EU data must remain in EU region during evaluation; can you confirm Redwood will run the eval on EU-hosted Dedicated nodes or a private VPC?
- For Japanese/Korean, we care more about intent precision than recall (false positives drive costly escalations).

Let's tentatively lock 3/25 10:00 CET for the sync — Kenji on our APAC team will join if timing works.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of ML Platforms | Globex Retail
anna.muller@globex.de

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@globex.de>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Anna — thanks for the clarifications. To confirm: we will run the initial evals in your requested EU region (Dedicated EU pool) to meet data residency requirements. We have two technical notes and a small ask from your data team before we start: 

1) Model choices and tradeoffs (short):
   - redwood-multilingual-2.0: highest cross-lingual intent accuracy in our benchmarks. Expect slightly higher latency but best-in-class quality for DE/FR/ES.
   - rwd-quant-4bit-multilang: similar intent F1 on JA/KO at a fraction of compute cost; can be used for inference tiering (EU traffic -> redwood-multilingual-2.0, non-critical high-volume APAC -> rwd-quant-4bit).

2) Quality regression concerns:
   - When we quantize heavily for throughput, we sometimes see regressed edge-case handling for rare idioms in DE/FR. We'll include targeted stress tests for those in the eval (see "rare-idioms" tab in prompt-sets.csv).
   - For Japanese, tokenization differences across toolchains can cause subtle label drift; we recommend a 200-example locale-focused eval for JA/KO after the first pass.

3) Small ask: please upload the anonymized file to the shared Drive folder or provide S3 with temporary credentials. Include a README with locale column and the canonical intent label set.

Workplan and deliverables by 3/25 sync: 
- Per-locale confusion matrices and top-10 error buckets (by intent).
- Latency p95 on Dedicated EU config and cost estimate for each model.
- Short recommendation for an initial rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%).

I'll run the first batch once we have the sample. Attaching checklist and the eval-run script snippet in the Drive.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

---
Attachment: eval-run-checklist.md (stored in Drive)
Attachment: prompt-sets.csv

From: Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@sumitomo.jp>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T10:43:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Morning — 3/25 10:00 CET works for me (I'll join from Tokyo). Looking forward to the per-locale breakdown; we are especially interested in the JA/KO results and any recommended prompt engineering to improve precision.

Kenji
